title: SLO-aware error surface catalog and remediation journey
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a consumable catalog ("Error Surface Catalog") that maps observed error signals to SLO exposure, automated remediation guidance, and the required telemetry for deterministic triage. The catalog will power a new dashboard view (Error Surface Grid) and a remediation journey in the Console that guides on-call engineers and automated runbooks through diagnostics and mitigation steps. This ticket covers design, tracehook enrichment, metric/log pipeline changes, dashboard authoring, and a minimal set of alert/playbook integrations.
acceptance_criteria: A searchable Error Surface Catalog exists in Confluence with taxonomy categories: client timeouts, backend timeouts, queue/overload, model rejection (generation errors, OOM), HTTP/gRPC error mappings, and infrastructure errors.

Tracehook instrumentation is shipping to capture required attributes per request: route, model_version, capacity_tier, queue_depth, batch_size, kv_cache_hits, inference_exit_mode, upstream_http_code, upstream_grpc_code.
Metric & log pipeline includes new labels and histogram buckets; dashboards display SLO-weighted error slices and can filter by model, region, and capacity tier.

Remediation journey UI presents recommended actions (retry with backoff, route to fallback model, reduce batch size, add capacity) and links to runbooks; each recommendation includes estimated mitigation time and SLO delta.
Automated alert rule prototypes for two high-impact slices (p95 latency spike causing SLO exposure; model_rejection rate spike) are created in Grafana/Alertmanager and smoke-tested in staging.
Docs and runbooks linked from the dashboard; at least one on-call triage has validated the flow in a simulated incident.
notes: Motivation: current observability surfaces show symptom counts but not SLO exposure or structured remediation. We need a deterministic mapping (error->impact->remediation) so triage time is reduced and runbooks can be partially automated. Scope deliberately excludes full automation of remediations (circuit-breaker replacements) — this ticket focuses on telemetry, UI, and guidance. Implementation will be staged: (1) taxonomy + tracehook additions, (2) pipeline & storage changes, (3) dashboard + UI, (4) alerting + runbook validation.

decisions: Use a small set of enumerated error_class values to keep storage efficient: TIMEOUT_CLIENT, TIMEOUT_BACKEND, OVERLOAD_QUEUE, MODEL_REJECTION, INFRA_HTTP, INFRA_GRPC, KERNEL_OOM, UNKNOWN.
Represent SLO exposure as a normalized score per error instance (0.0-1.0) and sum per slice to compare across routes/models.
Avoid per-request high-cardinality tags like exact batch_size; instead capture bucketed batch_size (1,2-4,5-8,9+).
Histogram buckets for request latency will be aligned with SLO boundaries: [0,50,100,250,500,1000,2000,5000] ms.
For initial rollout we keep remediation actions advisory (UI + links to runbooks) rather than executing automated mitigation.
Store enriched logs in the ELK cluster for 30d; metrics with SLO-weighting in Prometheus/Thanos with 90d retention for aggregate queries.
Adopt OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where possible for trace attributes to ease cross-team consumption.
